capitals.note: Fief from Beta I and 'later became the Kakatiya capital'; twin town of Warangal, a few kilometres away. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Warangal, nudged.

capitals.note: 'established in 1195'; renamed Sultanpur by Delhi after 1323.

rulers.note: 'r. c. 1199-1262'; Sircar gives 1260; alive in 1269 per a Duggi inscription

rulers.title: queen regnant
rulers.note: co-regent from c. 1260, sole ruler by 1263, anointed by 1269; killed in November 1289 (before 27 November)

correction.text: the Telangana region, where the Kakatiyas 'assumed sovereignty under Rudradeva in 1163 CE by suppressing other Chalukya subordinates', seat Anumakonda (Hanamkonda)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Kakatiya row starts in 1177, fourteen years after the 1163 sovereignty. The pages describe the early state only as the Telangana region; nothing on them dates Rudra's other conquests before 1199.

keyframe_review.note: 255,291 km2 (933 cells) for 1177-1187. The page gives no km2 figure for the kingdom, so no area check is possible. The shape includes the delta (about 300 cells); the ledger gains of 1201 and 1231 add it back. The Chhattisgarh and southern Odisha lobe is unverified before the 1212 Kalinga campaigns. The Rudradeva page (opened on the repair pass): Rudra's 1163 inscription claims a kingdom from the Godavari to the Srisailam area and from Kalyani to the Bay of Bengal, which the page calls an exaggeration, and it dates none of his conquests, so the 1177 shape's lobe outside Telangana (Kalinga, Chhattisgarh, southern Odisha, north coastal Andhra) is still undated.

keyframe_review.note: 254,934 km2 for 1188-1259. No infobox km2 to compare. The page shows the real shape moving inside this span: Velanadu by 1201, Kolanu in 1231, Kalinga lost 'sometime before 1217', Nellore lost in 1263. The ledger carries each step; the base shape is the part that holds from 1188.

minus.text: the western and southern land Cliopatria adds in 1260: the Raichur Doab and Bellary side of Karnataka, Kurnool and the Rayalaseema side, a strip of western Telangana

union.text: Cliopatria's 1260 shape without its western and southern additions, which no page opened places under the Kakatiyas before the 1294 Raichur Fort inscription

the Kadapa country, gained at 1239 and lost to Ambadeva at 1281 (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1260 shape without its western and southern additions (dated by the 1294 Raichur Fort inscription), plus the Kadapa country the Kakatiyas hold from 1239 until Ambadeva breaks away

keyframe_review.note: 297,558 km2 for 1260-1313: a 402-cell lobe (Karnataka 235, Andhra Pradesh 84, Telangana 64, Maharashtra 19) is added against 1188. The Prataparudra II page: a 1294 Raichur Fort inscription says Gona Vithala captured forts in Bellary district and the Raichur Doab; the Kakatiya page puts the peak extent 'from close to Anagondi in the west to Kalyani in the north-east, and down to Kanei and Ganjam district' without a year, so the shape reads as the peak extent set at the end of Ganapati's reign. No infobox km2. Nellore falls to the Pandyas in 1263 (ledger). Repair pass: the Kadapa country (96 cells, only 16 inside Cliopatria's 1188 shape) is added because the Gandikota page has the Kakatiyas ruling Gandikota from 1239 and the Rudrama Devi page makes Ambadeva's principality a part of their south-western territory; the 1239 gain and the 1281 loss carry it.

union.text: the Kadapa country, annexed in 1309 (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1314 shape plus the Kadapa country (Mulikinadu) annexed from the Kayastha principality in 1309; it holds for 1314-1322 only

keyframe_review.note: 297,558 km2, the same outline as 1260. The years change: Cliopatria runs the row to 1325, the Prataparudra II page has the dynasty end in 1323. Tributary status to Delhi from 1310 is not a change of outline. The Prataparudra II page says Kampili forces had seized the western part of the Kakatiya kingdom, without a year, and the Kampili page does not mention it, so the western part is left in the shape (unverified). Repair pass: Cliopatria's Kakatiya shape holds only 31 of the 96 cells of the Kadapa country the page has annexed in 1309, so the rest is added here; the 1290 regain of Nellore and the 1294 gains bring the ledger to the outline of the 1314 shape.

region.text: the Telangana region, with Anumakonda (Hanamkonda) as the seat

ledger.note: 1163: the Kakatiyas, under Rudradeva, end their feudatory status and rule Telangana from Anumakonda (Hanamkonda). 'They assumed sovereignty under Rudradeva in 1163 CE by suppressing other Chalukya subordinates in the Telangana region'; the 1163 Anumakonda inscription 'is the earliest known record that describes the Kakatiyas as a sovereign power'. The infobox says 'Established: 1163'. Cliopatria's row starts only in 1177; the western-chalukya-empire dossier records the matching 1163 loss of Telangana.

1195: the capital moves from Anumakonda (Hanamkonda) to Orugallu (Warangal). 'The Kakatiya capital at Orugallu, established in 1195, was not forgotten while Ganapati expanded his territory.' The Ganapati Deva page adds that Ganapati 'continued Rudra-deva's project of moving the capital from Anumakonda to Orugallu' and fortified it, so the move was gradual; the two towns are a few kilometres apart.

region.text: the Kakatiya-Yadava frontier of the Telangana marches

ledger.note: 1198: Yadava (Seuna) armies fight the Kakatiyas on the Telangana frontier. The Ganapati Deva page has Mahadeva, Ganapati's father, die fighting the Seunas in 1198-1199. The yadava-dynasty dossier (Seuna page) dates the Yadava invasion under Jaitugi to 'around 1194'. No page opened names the front, so the zone is the frontier band.

region.text: the Kakatiya-Yadava frontier of the Telangana marches

ledger.note: 1199: Mahadeva dies and Ganapati Deva ('r. c. 1199-1262') takes the throne; the fighting with the Yadavas ends. The Yadava suzerainty the Singhana II page (see yadava-dynasty) reports for these years is drawn in the yadava-dynasty dossier as a vassal relation (Singhana II page: appointed 1198; 'the second half of his reign' independent), not here.

region.text: Vela-nadu, Kamma-nadu and the Krishna delta

ledger.note: 1201: the Kakatiyas hold the Krishna delta and Vela-nadu. 'The Kakatiyas conquered this region by 1201, as attested by the 1201 CE Kanaka-durga temple inscription'; 'By 1209, Ganapati had annexed the Vela-nadu and the Karmma-rashtra (Kamma-nadu) regions to his kingdom.' 1201 is the latest date by which the conquest is attested, so the year is a bound. The chola-empire dossier carries Cliopatria's 1177 bridge for the same land.

region.text: Nellore

ledger.note: 1208: Ganapati installs Tikka at Nellore. 'Ganapati marched to Nellore, forced Tammu-siddhi to flee, and installed Tikka on the throne as Tikka-bhupala.' The page gives no year for this; it says only that Nalla-siddhi and Tammu-siddhi 'ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208', so 1208 is a bridge (page silent). Tikka died in 1248.

region.text: Kalinga: the north-eastern lobe of Cliopatria's 1188 shape (Chhattisgarh, southern Odisha, the Visakhapatnam side) that its 1260 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 1212: Kakatiya campaigns reach Kalinga. 'After his successes in Kalinga, Raja-nayaka marched to Draksharamam' and 'made a gift ... to the god Bhimeshvara in 1212 CE'. The page gives no year for the Kalinga successes themselves, so 1212 is the latest date by which the campaign had taken ground.

region.text: Kalinga: the north-eastern lobe of Cliopatria's 1188 shape (Chhattisgarh, southern Odisha, the Visakhapatnam side) that its 1260 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 1217: the Eastern Ganga king expels the Kakatiyas from Kalinga. 'Sometime before 1217 CE, Ananga Bhima III ... expelled Kakatiya forces from Kalinga.' The year is the page's bound.

region.text: Kalinga: the north-eastern lobe of Cliopatria's 1188 shape (Chhattisgarh, southern Odisha, the Visakhapatnam side) that its 1260 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 1217: Kalinga is lost. After the expulsion 'The Kakatiya control was likely limited to the south of the Godavari River'; the 1236 Upparapalli inscription credits Raja-nayaka with capturing Udayagiri (a raid, not a lasting gain). Cliopatria's 1188 shape reaches north of the Godavari and its 1260 shape drops this lobe; the eastern-ganga-kingdom dossier draws its own gain at 1260, so the date differs by the page's reading.

region.text: Kolanu in the Vengi region

ledger.note: 1231: the Kakatiyas conquer Kolanu in Vengi. 'A 1231 CE Paleshvara temple (Iragavaram) inscription confirms the Kakatiya conquest of Kolanu in Vengi region in that year.' The page names no state that held Kolanu; the region drawn is the Vengi doab, my reading of 'Vengi region'. The chola-empire dossier has Vengi leaving the Chola shape at 1177 (a Cliopatria bridge, confidence 1).

region.text: the Kadapa country, ruled by Kakatiya subordinates from 1239 (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

ledger.note: 1239: the Kadapa country comes under Kakatiya rule. The Gandikota page: 'Gandikota came under the rule of Kakatiya dynasty from 1239 A.D to 1304 A.D and ruled by their various subordinates.' The year is the page's; the page is a village article and speaks of one fort, so the Kadapa-country region is my reading (confidence 2). The Rudrama Devi page supports the land: Ambadeva's principality was carved out of the 'former south-western parts' of the Kakatiya territory south of the Krishna, and Rudrama regained 'some of the territory' lost to the Pandyas (inscriptions of 1264 and 1268). Cliopatria's 1188 shape holds only 16 of the 96 cells of the radius. The page names no previous holder, hence 'nobody'.

region.text: Nellore

ledger.note: 1263: Manuma-siddhi II, the Telugu Choda ruler of Nellore, is killed at Muttukuru and the line ends: 'The Pandyas captured Nellore, and killed Manuma-siddhi II in the Battle of Muttukuru in 1263 CE.'

region.text: Nellore and the southernmost Kakatiya land

ledger.note: 1263: the Pandyas take Nellore. 'The Pandyas captured Nellore, and killed Manuma-siddhi II in the Battle of Muttukuru in 1263 CE.' The Rudrama Devi page says that toward the end of Ganapati's reign the Pandyas took the southernmost Kakatiya land, including Nellore, and that Rudrama's forces later regained some of it in Kadapa and Nellore (undated). Cliopatria keeps Nellore in the Kakatiya shape throughout.

region.text: Nellore

ledger.note: 1271: Naga-deva rules Nellore under Rudrama. Naga-deva ruled Nellore from 1271 to 1275 as her vassal (the page's statement, closely paraphrased). This is how the page records the partial recovery of the south after the Pandya conquest.

region.text: Vengi

ledger.note: c. 1274: the Eastern Ganga prince Bhanudeva I invades Vengi. Narasimha I's son Bhanudeva I 'invaded Vengi around 1274 CE'; Rudrama's generals Poti and Proli Nayaka 'repulsed the Gajapatis, restoring Kakatiya control of coastal Andhra south of the Godavari.' The page names the invader as a Gajapati; the eastern-ganga-kingdom row is the nearest Cliopatria state.

region.text: Vengi

ledger.note: The invasion is repulsed. The page gives no year for the repulse, so the end shares the start year (page silent; confidence 1).

region.text: Nellore

ledger.note: 1275: Naga-deva's rule at Nellore ends (he ruled from 1271 to 1275 per the page). The page then has the Telugu Choda Tiru-kalatti-deva II (c. 1279-1283) and Ambadeva's nominee Manuma Ganda-gopala on the Nellore throne, neither as a Kakatiya vassal.

union.text: Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre

the Tripurantakam area of Prakasam district, where Ambadeva's inscriptions of 1273 and 1290 stand and his last record is dated 13 June 1291; the place is not in the gazetteer and the coordinates are approximate

region.text: Ambadeva's principality when it breaks away: the Kadapa country of the 1287 Attirala inscription and the Tripurantakam area

ledger.note: before 1281: Ambadeva's Kayastha principality breaks away with the Kadapa country and the Tripurantakam area. The Rudrama Devi page has Ambadeva become chief in 1272, initially loyal but later asserting independence, and carving out an independent principality that included 'almost all of the former south-western parts' of the Kakatiya territory south of the Krishna River; the Ambadeva page lists its places in the 1287 Attirala inscription. No page opened dates the break, so 1281, the latest date by which he is attested (Manuma Ganda-gopala on the Nellore throne 'Sometime before 1281'), is the year (confidence 1). Nellore is NOT part of the loss: it was a Telugu Choda throne (Tiru-kalatti-deva II c. 1279-1283, then Ambadeva's nominee), not Kakatiya land, and the kayastha dossier records it as a vassal. The principality has no Cliopatria row; its dossier is a rebel state.

region.text: Nellore and the southernmost Kakatiya land lost to the Pandyas in 1263, as far as Cliopatria's 1314 outline

ledger.note: 1290: the Kakatiyas retake Nellore. 'In 1290 CE, Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore.' Manuma-Gandagopala was 'another Choda chief' (Rudrama Devi page), so the counterpart is the Telugu Chodas; kayastha-principality-of-ambadeva records the end of its vassal relation. An earlier draft had c. 1298 (confidence 1), the year of a 1297-98 inscription on the Prataparudra II page, which belongs to the later expedition against Raja-Gandagopala's Pandya alliance. The 1263 loss was drawn with a 120 km radius, so the regain takes the same land (restricted to the Cliopatria outline).

region.text: the Kadapa country and Mulikinadu, to which Ambadeva 'had to retreat southwards' (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

ledger.note: 1291: Prataparudra's army marches on Ambadeva. 'In 1291-92 (Shaka 1213), Prataparudra sent an army to Tripurantakam' and Ambadeva 'had to retreat southwards to the Mulikinadu region' (Prataparudra II page). Rudrama had been 'killed in November 1289 CE by Amba-deva's forces' (Rudrama Devi page). No page records fighting between 1291 and 1309; the contest is kept open to the 1309 expedition because the Kayastha rule lasted until then. The region is the Kadapa country, which replaces an earlier Ongole radius that no page names.

region.text: the Tripurantakam area of Prakasam district, where Ambadeva's inscriptions of 1273 and 1290 stand and his last record is dated 13 June 1291; the place is not in the gazetteer and the coordinates are approximate

ledger.note: mid-1291: the Kakatiyas take Tripurantakam. A Kakatiya force 'defeated him in mid-1291'; Ambadeva's 'last record at Tripurantakam is dated 13 June 1291' and 'the earliest record of Manuma-Gannaya and Annaya-deva at the place is dated 11 August 1291' (Ambadeva page; the Prataparudra II page has the army sent to Tripurantakam in 1291-92). The page gives no month. kayastha-principality-of-ambadeva carries the matching loss.

union.text: the Karnataka land north of the Tungabhadra up to the Malaprabha and Krishna, Dharwad and Belgaum side
Anantapur, Bellary, Chitradurga, Shimoga and most of Dharwad

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1260 Kakatiya additions that the Yadava dossier holds (Cliopatria's 1236 Yadava shape and the 1212 gain): the Raichur Doab, Bellary, the Gulbarga and Bidar side and Kurnool

ledger.note: 1294: Gona Vithala takes Raichur. The page: a 1294 Raichur Fort inscription says Gona Vithala captured forts in Bellary district and the Raichur Doab, and took the city of Raichur. The rest of this land is Cliopatria's 1260 additions that the yadava-dynasty dossier holds in 1236 (Kurnool and the Rayalaseema side, western Telangana), which the Ramachandra page (opened for yadava-dynasty) says Prataparudra annexed from the Yadavas after 1296 ('the eastern part of Ramachandra's kingdom, which included the present-day Anantapur and Raichur districts'); this page does not date them, so the lobe is drawn at 1294 (region is my reading, confidence 2). yadava-dynasty carries the matching loss; the cells of the lobe that no Yadava shape holds are the next event.

union.text: the Karnataka land north of the Tungabhadra up to the Malaprabha and Krishna, Dharwad and Belgaum side
Anantapur, Bellary, Chitradurga, Shimoga and most of Dharwad

Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre

the Tripurantakam area of Prakasam district, where Ambadeva's inscriptions of 1273 and 1290 stand and his last record is dated 13 June 1291; the place is not in the gazetteer and the coordinates are approximate

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's 1260 Kakatiya additions: Kurnool, Nandyal and the Mahbubnagar side, minus Nellore (gained in 1290) and the Kadapa country (gained in 1309)

ledger.note: c. 1294: about 50 cells of Cliopatria's 1260 Kakatiya additions are in no Yadava shape of the yadava-dynasty dossier and in no event of this one; the Prataparudra II page gives only the 1294 Raichur Fort inscription and the Ramachandra page 'after 1296' for the Yadava land. Who held these cells before is on no page opened, so they are drawn as a confidence-1 bridge from nobody at the same year as the neighbouring lobe (page silent).

region.text: Mulikinadu and the Kadapa country (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

ledger.note: 1309: Prataparudra ends the Kayastha rule. 'In 1309, Prataparudra sent an expedition to Mulikinadu, which resulted in the end of the Kayastha rule.' The year is the page's; the drawn region is the Kadapa country, which is my reading of the Mulikinadu the page names (the Ambadeva page lists Muliki-nadu among the places of the principality), so confidence 2.

region.text: Mulikinadu and the Kadapa country (Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre)

ledger.note: 1309: Mulikinadu is annexed. 'In 1309, Prataparudra sent an expedition to Mulikinadu, which resulted in the end of the Kayastha rule.' The page adds that 'The region was annexed to the Kakatiya kingdom'. Year and name are the page's; the Kadapa-country region is my reading, so confidence 2. An earlier draft drew a 120 km radius round Ongole, which no page names and which overlapped the 1201 Vela-nadu gain.

region.text: Orugallu (Warangal) and its fort

ledger.note: January 1310: Malik Kafur besieges Orugallu. 'Kafur organised a month-long siege of Orugallu that ended with success in February 1310' (the January start is inferred from 'month-long'). The 1303 raid had failed at Upparapalli.

region.text: Orugallu (Warangal) and its fort

ledger.note: February 1310: Prataparudra submits. 'After the successful siege of Warangal in 1310, Prataparudra II was forced to pay annual tribute to Delhi.' The page names no land lost; the tribute relation is for the khalji-dynasty dossier's vassal events.

region.text: Kanchi

ledger.note: c. 1317: Kakatiya forces occupy Kanchi. 'After Alauddin's death in 1316, the Hoysala king Ballala launched a fresh invasion' of Pandya territory; the Kakatiya commander Peda Rudra defeated Ballala, and the Kakatiyas then occupied Kanchi; Devarinayaka's 1317 grant came after he defeated Vira Pandya and reinstated Sundara Pandya. The source says Prataparudra gained no lasting benefit.

region.text: Orugallu (Warangal) and its fort

ledger.note: 1318: Khusrau Khan marches on Warangal. 'In 1318, he failed to provide the annual tribute to Delhi'; Khusrau Khan returned with siege technology.

region.text: Orugallu (Warangal) and its fort

ledger.note: 1318: Prataparudra submits again. 'The amount of his annual tribute was changed, becoming 100 elephants and 12,000 horses.' The Prataparudra II page adds that he 'agreed to cede five districts of his kingdom to Mubarak Shah' without naming them; the Kakatiya page does not mention a cession, so none is drawn. The Siege of Warangal (1318) article says Khusrau Khan demanded five districts (Badarkot, Kailas, Basudan, Elor and Kobar) and that the settlement ceded only Badarkot, with annual tribute cut to 40 gold bricks; none of these places is in the gazetteer, so nothing is drawn.

region.text: Kanchi

ledger.note: 1323: the Kanchi occupation ends with the kingdom. No page opened dates the end of the occupation (page silent; confidence 1).

region.text: Orugallu (Warangal) and its fort

ledger.note: 1323: Ulugh Khan (Jauna Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughluq) returns to Orugallu after the failure of 1321 and besieges it for five months ('Within four months ... besieged the fort again', Prataparudra II page).

region.text: Orugallu (Warangal) and its fort

ledger.note: 9 November 1323: the siege of Warangal ends and Prataparudra is 'forced into submission'.

region.text: the whole Kakatiya kingdom

ledger.note: 1323: the Kakatiya kingdom is annexed to the Delhi Sultanate. The conquest 'resulted in the annexation of their kingdom to the Delhi Sultanate'; Orugallu was renamed Sultanpur (Kakatiya dynasty page).

region.text: the Kakatiya kingdom at its fall

ledger.note: 9 November 1323: the Kakatiya dynasty ends with the fall of Warangal. Prataparudra was taken toward Delhi and probably died near the Narmada. The Musunuri Nayakas recovered Warangal from Delhi 'as early as 1330' (see successors).

wars.name: Yadava invasion of the Kakatiya country

zones.text: the Kakatiya-Yadava frontier of the Telangana marches

wars.outcome: Mahadeva died fighting the Seunas in 1198-1199 and Ganapati Deva succeeded; no land is recorded as changing hands.
wars.note: The yadava-dynasty dossier (Seuna and Singhana II pages) has Jaitugi invading 'around 1194' and installing Ganapati as a Yadava vassal in 1198; that suzerainty is not on this dossier's pages.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of Vela-nadu and the Krishna delta
wars.outcome: The Kakatiyas held the region by 1201 and had annexed Vela-nadu and Karmma-rashtra by 1209.
wars.note: The Velanati Chodas (a Chola feudatory line) have no Cliopatria row; a dossier is flagged.

wars.name: Kakatiya campaigns in Kalinga

zones.text: Kalinga: the north-eastern lobe of Cliopatria's 1188 shape (Chhattisgarh, southern Odisha, the Visakhapatnam side) that its 1260 shape no longer holds

wars.outcome: Ananga Bhima III expelled the Kakatiya forces from Kalinga sometime before 1217; Kakatiya control stayed south of the Godavari.
wars.note: The Upparapalli inscription of 1236 credits Raja-nayaka with taking Udayagiri; the page treats the Godavari-Kalinga battle as after 1248. Neither moved the border.

wars.name: Kakatiya raid on Kanchi
wars.outcome: The 1228 Mattevada inscription says Ganapati 'plundered the Chola capital', probably Kanchi; no land was taken.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of Kolanu
wars.outcome: The Iragavaram inscription of 1231 confirms the Kakatiya conquest of Kolanu in Vengi that year.

wars.name: Pandya conquest of Nellore
wars.outcome: Around 1257 Jatavarman Sundara I subdued the Chola king and Kanchi; the Pandyas captured Nellore and killed Manuma-siddhi II at Muttukuru in 1263. Rudrama later regained some of the south (undated).
wars.note: Ganapati 'apparently retired after suffering defeats against the Pandyas in the late 1250s'.

wars.name: Eastern Ganga and Gajapati invasion of Vengi
wars.outcome: Bhanudeva I invaded Vengi around 1274 and was repulsed by Poti and Proli Nayaka, who restored Kakatiya control south of the Godavari.

wars.name: Ambadeva's Kayastha revolt

zones.text: Valluru-pattana, Gandikota, Muliki-nadu, Renadu, Pendekallu, Sakili, Eruva and Pottapi-nadu, the places in Ambadeva's 1287 Attirala inscription (Ambadeva page): the Kadapa country of Rayalaseema; Proddatur, in the heart of Renadu (Renadu page), stands in as its centre

the Tripurantakam area of Prakasam district, where Ambadeva's inscriptions of 1273 and 1290 stand and his last record is dated 13 June 1291; the place is not in the gazetteer and the coordinates are approximate

wars.outcome: Ambadeva, chief from 1272, set up an independent principality south of the Krishna (the Kadapa country and Tripurantakam), killed Rudrama in November 1289 (a theory on indirect evidence), lost Nellore to Prataparudra in 1290 and Tripurantakam in mid-1291, and the Kayastha rule in Mulikinadu ended with the expedition of 1309.
wars.note: The Prataparudra II page dates the army sent to Tripurantakam to 1291-92, Ambadeva's retreat 'southwards to the Mulikinadu region' and the end of Kayastha rule to 1309; the Rudrama Devi page has the principality carved from the Kakatiyas' south-western lands.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of the Raichur Doab

zones.text: the western and southern land Cliopatria adds in 1260: the Raichur Doab and Bellary side of Karnataka, Kurnool and the Rayalaseema side, a strip of western Telangana

wars.outcome: Gona Vithala took forts in Bellary district, the Raichur Doab and the city of Raichur in 1294; the zone is Cliopatria's 1260 additions.

wars.name: Khalji invasions of Warangal
wars.outcome: The 1303 raid by Malik Chajju and Fakhruddin Jauna failed at Upparapalli; Malik Kafur's month-long siege ended in February 1310 with annual tribute; Khusrau Khan's 1318 expedition raised the tribute to 100 elephants and 12,000 horses. No annexation.
wars.note: The Prataparudra II page dates the 1303 invasion 'late 1302 or early 1303' and has five districts ceded in 1318; the Kakatiya page does not.

wars.name: Tughluq conquest of the Kakatiya kingdom
wars.outcome: Jauna Khan was repulsed in 1321 and retreated to Devagiri; he returned in 1323, besieged Orugallu for five months and Prataparudra surrendered on 9 November 1323; the kingdom was annexed.
wars.note: The Prataparudra II page has Ulugh Khan return 'within four months'.

wars.name: Kakatiya intervention in the Pandya civil war
wars.outcome: Peda Rudra defeated the Hoysala king Ballala, defeated Vira Pandya and reinstated Sundara Pandya; the Kakatiyas occupied Kanchi but, per the page, gained no lasting benefit.

certainty.note: Kakatiya frontiers rest on inscription find-spots and claims (Anagondi to Kalyani at the peak); no treaty line is recorded. The Godavari is the page's frontier with Kalinga after 1217.

The tribute settlements of 1310 and 1318 fix no boundary; the Siege of Warangal (1318) article names the five demanded districts (Badarkot, Kailas, Basudan, Elor, Kobar) and says only Badarkot was ceded, none in the gazetteer, so nothing is drawn.

sources.title: Kakatiya dynasty
sources.note: Identity, 1163 sovereignty, capitals, rulers, 1310 and 1318 Delhi tribute, 1323 end; no km2 figure.

sources.title: Ganapati Deva
sources.note: Velanadu by 1201, Nellore, Kalinga before 1217, Kolanu 1231, Pandya conquest of Nellore 1263.

sources.title: Rudrama Devi
sources.note: Succession 1263 and death November 1289, Pandya and Gajapati wars, Ambadeva, Nellore vassals 1271-1275. Repair pass: Naga-deva 'a vassal of Rudrama' at Nellore 1271-1275 (not called a Choda); Tiru-kalatti-deva II (Choda) c. 1279-1283; Manuma Ganda-gopala appointed before 1281.

sources.title: Prataparudra II
sources.note: Reign to 1323, Ambadeva's end 1309, Raichur 1294, Delhi invasions, Kanchi, annexation 1323.

sources.title: Kampili kingdom
sources.note: Thin: founding 1280-1300 by a Hoysala commander, fall in 1327; says nothing about Kakatiya or Yadava land, so the Kampili seizure of the western Kakatiya land stays undated.

sources.title: Ambadeva
sources.note: Chief 1272, capital Valluru-pattana, the 1287 Attirala list, Nellore 1290, defeat in mid-1291; silent on 1291-1309.

sources.title: Gandikota
sources.note: Gandikota 'came under the rule of Kakatiya dynasty from 1239 A.D to 1304 A.D and ruled by their various subordinates'; coordinates 14.81472N 78.28667E.

sources.title: Renadu
sources.note: Heart of Renadu: Nossam, Uyyalawada, Koilkuntla, Owk, Jammalamadugu and Proddatur; read for the region name only.

sources.title: Rudradeva
sources.note: Rudra: sovereignty 1163, last record 26 April 1195 (Bekkallu inscription), no years for his conquests; the 1163 inscription's claimed extent is called an exaggeration.

sources.title: Siege of Warangal (1318)
sources.note: Five districts demanded (Badarkot, Kailas, Basudan, Elor, Kobar); only Badarkot ceded; annual tribute cut to 40 gold bricks.

notes:
See history/polities/_notes/sa-03-h.md. Cliopatria's Kakatiya row (1177..1325) is corrected in four ways: it starts 14 years after the 1163 sovereignty; it draws the Krishna-Godavari delta from 1177 although the Ganapati Deva page has it conquered by 1201 and 1231; its 1260 shape is the peak extent of Ganapati's reign set at the end of his reign, with the western lobe (Raichur Doab, Bellary, Kurnool side) dated by the 1294 Raichur Fort inscription; and it runs two years past the fall of 1323. Unverified: the Chhattisgarh and southern Odisha lobe of the 1177-1259 shape, Gulbarga and Bidar in the 1294 lobe (the page says only 'Kalyani in the north-east'), the western Kakatiya land Kampili seized, and the five districts of 1318. Tribute to Delhi from 1310 is left to the khalji-dynasty and tughlaq-dynasty dossiers (vassal_start with counterpart kakatiya-dynasty). The Kakatiya page's 'Kalyani in the north-east' sits oddly with Kalyani being north-west of Warangal.

Repair pass 2026-10-19 (reviewer: fail). Ambadeva's land is now the Kadapa country (Proddatur 90 km, the 1287 Attirala list on the Ambadeva page) plus the Tripurantakam area, not Ongole 120 km; the Kadapa country is added to the shape from 1239 (Gandikota page) so that the 1281 loss and the 1309 gain are land the dossier holds. Nellore is no longer lost in 1281 (it was a Telugu Choda throne under Ambadeva's nominee, a vassal of Ambadeva) and is retaken in 1290 (Ambadeva page; the 1298 date was the year of a later inscription). Tripurantakam is gained in mid-1291. The 1294 lobe is split: the part the Yadava dossier holds (counterpart yadava-dynasty) and about 50 cells no Yadava shape holds (nobody, confidence 1). Counterparts 'Rulers of Kolanu in Vengi' (the page names a Maha-mandaleshvara Kolani Keshava-deva) and 'Naga-deva of Nellore' (the page calls him 'a vassal of Rudrama', not a Choda) are listed as counterparts needing dossiers; the Nellore Chodas now use the slug telugu-chodas-of-nellore. Disagreement kept: the Rudrama Devi page also says Tiru-kalatti-deva II 'appears to have displaced Naga-deva from Nellore in 1263', which does not fit Naga-deva's 1271-1275 rule on the same page; the ledger follows 1271-1275. The Gandikota page says the Kakatiyas held Gandikota to 1304, which does not fit the 1281 break; read as nominal rule through subordinates. Kampili page re-read on the repair pass: it says nothing of Kakatiya or Warangal land (it places the kingdom 'near Ballari', founded by a Hoysala commander 1280-1300, fallen 1327), so the western land Kumara Rama seized (Prataparudra II page, no year) stays undated and in the shape. The Rudradeva page dates none of Rudra's conquests, so the Kalinga and Chhattisgarh lobe of the 1177 shape stays unverified. Confidence-1 bridges left (pages silent): Tikka at Nellore 1208, the end of the 1274 Vengi contest (Bhanudeva I invaded Vengi 'around 1274', Rudrama Devi page), the end of the Kanchi occupation.
